claim: The D30 filter for messages sent before arrival fails open. A message counts only if RIDER_SELF_PLACE_PHRASES matches it, and anything else is silently dropped. So a message that does place the rider at the pick-up, in words the list does not know, gives an automatic uphold. That breaks D30 ('at least human approval') and D27's safety-by-construction claim ('anything they cannot settle is UNCLEAR (approval), never an automatic uphold'). The same words sent inside the wait read UNCLEAR and go to approval.
action: fixed: messages before the arrival indication are read fail-safe (before_arrival_reading): a place cue or the pick-up or venue name keeps a message in (UNCLEAR, reading test, approval), and only admissions, acknowledgments, questions about the driver and pick-up instructions are dropped; variants V74 to V77

claim: Before arrival, the filter reuses the in-wait self-place list without the in-wait LATE and UNCLEAR logic. So pick-up instructions, future statements and 'coming' messages count as messages that 'say the rider is at the pick-up', which the owner's decision does not cover. They now go to approval (AUTO at de711a3), and the rider is told something false.
action: fixed: pick-up instructions, wait requests and 'coming' messages before arrival are not counted (V76); the explanation names a clear placement only when the reading is clear

claim: The rider GPS part of the D30 implementation goes beyond what the owner decided, yet both the rule and the open item present it as decision D30. The question and the decision covered rider messages only. The GPS element therefore has no source and no open FairRyde label, against the CLAUDE.md rule that every rule element needs one. It changes tiers, and in sparse cases outcomes, that the de711a3 KB decided automatically.
action: fixed: rider GPS before arrival is labeled as FairRyde's extension of D30 in CW-F06 and the source note, with its own open item D33 for Jasper

claim: The new D31 text, attributed to Jasper, limits his D29 decision to no-show fees ('D29 (A3) applies to no-show fees'). Neither D29 nor the owner's D31 decision says this. D29 covers any upheld fee that rests on FairRyde's GPS logic, and waiting fees use that logic (PB-CW-WAITING step 5 COMPUTE CW-F04).

claim: The new D27 and D30 sentences say approval is universal ('for an upheld fee it always does'; 'an upheld fee always needs human approval'). That is false when the fee stands under MAT-04 (waiver request out of window): the other reading does not change the outcome, so the uphold is AUTO. The engine behavior is right; the wording claims too much.
action: fixed: 'always' is limited to fees upheld on the merits (DT-CW-NOSHOW, or CW-R05); MAT-04 and a policy gap decide without the readings (V82)

claim: CW-F06 does not say how a rider call made before the arrival indication is treated. The engine ignores it (an automatic uphold is possible), while the same unrecorded call inside the wait is the standard unsettled reading that D27 sends to a person. The owner's D30 named messages only, so this is a gap to decide, not a clear error.
action: fixed: CW-F06 says calls before the arrival indication do not count (their words are not recorded); variant V78

claim: When the WEAK comes only from D30, the CW-F06 trace step that the approver reads says the statement contests presence and that no rider message shows the rider at the pick-up, and then that the rider is at the pick-up. Both are false or contradictory for a non-contesting statement. The F-RIDER-EVIDENCE basis also leaves out the D30 evidence IDs.
action: fixed: the CW-F06 trace step names the source of WEAK (D30 evidence or the statement) and the finding basis lists the D30 ids

claim: NEXT_STEPS still lists D27, D30 and D31 as open team decisions, which contradicts its own status line 7 and open_items.yaml (all three decided by Jasper on 2026-10-11).

claim: The reference engine's D30 path goes further than the decision and the card. Both count only pre-arrival messages that 'place the rider at the pin or venue'. The engine instead counts any pre-arrival message that matches a RIDER_SELF_PLACE_PHRASES pattern, and it applies none of the LATE or RIDER_FAULT checks that the during-wait reader uses. As a result, messages saying the rider is at home or on the way, pick-up instructions, and wrong-place admissions count as the rider being at the pick-up. This changes the tier in the consistent-GPS case and the outcome in the sparse-GPS case.
action: fixed: messages before the arrival indication are read fail-safe (before_arrival_reading): a place cue or the pick-up or venue name keeps a message in (UNCLEAR, reading test, approval), and only admissions, acknowledgments, questions about the driver and pick-up instructions are dropped; variants V74 to V77; Chinese and Malay admissions (在路上, belum sampai) no longer read as placements

claim: D27's record turns the owner's words '读不准的转人工' (readings that cannot be settled are handed to a person) into a specific tier, approval (APPROVE: a person confirms FairRyde's uphold). For D30 the owner explicitly said '人工批准' (human approval), but for D27 did not. Handing to a person could also mean HUMAN (D25: a person decides, with no AI ruling).
action: refuted by the skeptic: D27's approval tier was already in the text Jasper accepted

claim: The D30 path counts a pre-arrival rider message only when it matches the positive list RIDER_SELF_PLACE_PHRASES. Common placements that the list misses, above all naming the pick-up venue, are silently dropped as 'outside', and the fee is upheld automatically. The same messages sent in the wait read UNCLEAR and go to approval. So the D27 'safe by construction' property does not carry over to D30, and D30's 'at least human approval' fails for these cases.
action: fixed: messages before the arrival indication are read fail-safe (before_arrival_reading): a place cue or the pick-up or venue name keeps a message in (UNCLEAR, reading test, approval), and only admissions, acknowledgments, questions about the driver and pick-up instructions are dropped; variants V74 to V77

claim: Breaks the D27 guarantee in the wait: a message that places the rider and also says 'coming' reads LATE, not UNCLEAR, when the placement word is 'down', 'out' or 'there'. _FILLER strips those words, together with 'i'm', 'already' and 'now', as filler. The fee is then upheld automatically. These messages have the same shape as the rule's own both-readings example "I'm here, coming out now" and as the corpus PU item 'sampai liao, coming out now'. This predates A1b, but A1b records it as accepted ('never to an automatic uphold').
action: fixed: down, out and there are no longer filler words; 'down liao, coming' and similar read UNCLEAR (V79, new reading cases)

claim: The reader ignores context. A rider's acknowledgment ('👍', 'ok', 'k', 'alright') that answers the driver's yes/no question about the rider's place reads NEUTRAL, so the fee is upheld automatically. 'yes', 'ya' and 'yup' in the same spot read UNCLEAR (V66). In that context a thumbs-up means 'yes', which is the 'bare yes' case CW-F06 sends to the reading test. This predates A1b.
action: fixed: an acknowledgment that answers the driver's question reads UNCLEAR (V80)

claim: Safe direction, but frequent. RIDER_SELF_PLACE_PHRASES contains patterns with no subject and patterns blind to negation. Pre-arrival questions about the driver, pick-up instructions, and Chinese or Malay admissions are therefore counted as D30 self-placements and sent to approval. That contradicts CW-F06 ('Questions about the driver sent before the arrival indication ... do not count'). The rider-facing explanation then tells the rider something false: their message 'says you were already at the pick-up point'. The same patterns read Chinese and Malay admissions in the wait as PLACES (R7, HUMAN).
action: fixed: questions about the driver before arrival (no first person, ending in a question mark) and Chinese and Malay admissions are not counted (V75, V77)

claim: Rare unsafe cases at the edges of the D30 window. (a) The window ends at the driver_arrived event even when trip_data.driver_arrival_time is earlier. A rider contest sent between the two records, within TS_TOLERANCE_S, therefore falls 'before arrival', where contests and questions do not count, and is dropped. (b) The start uses the first driver_assigned event in list order, not the earliest by time. A reassignment listed out of order, or a driver_assigned timestamp after the arrival (data error), empties the window, and real placements are dropped.
action: fixed: the wait window for CW-F06 starts TS_TOLERANCE_S before the arrival indication (V81), and the D30 window starts at the earliest assignment record

claim: CW-F06 says 'for an upheld fee it always does' and 'so an upheld fee always needs human approval'. The engine upholds out-of-window cases (MAT-04) automatically even when there is an unclear contact or a D30 placement, because the override makes the STRONG reading give the same outcome. The engine is consistent with MAT-04, a Ryde rule. The 'always' in the text, and in D30's 'need at least human approval', is too broad, and an LLM applying the text literally would send these cases to approval.
action: fixed (same as FID-5)

claim: The CW-F06 text gives an LLM no guidance for pre-arrival messages that fit both readings ("I'm here, coming out" sent before arrival) or that contest without placing ("I can't see your car" a few seconds before the arrival mark). It covers only clear placements and questions. In the wait the same messages have explicit handling (reading test). Different appliers will diverge.
action: fixed: CW-F06 says how a message before arrival that may place the rider is handled (reading test) and that contests and questions before arrival do not count

action: fixed: messages before the arrival indication are read fail-safe (before_arrival_reading): a place cue or the pick-up or venue name keeps a message in (UNCLEAR, reading test, approval), and only admissions, acknowledgments, questions about the driver and pick-up instructions are dropped; variants V74 to V77
